description: Sinbad the Sailor: Seven Voyages, Monsters and Treasures. Behind the marvelous, the portrait of the merchant-adventurer of the Islamic golden age.

hero.hook: Seven times he leaves rich or curious. Seven times the sea breaks it. Seven times he comes back even richer.

blocks.text: **Sindbad the sailor** belongs to the **Arabian Nights**, but not to the old Persian core of the collection. His cycle of seven journeys took place later, in Egypt, around the 15th century.

He embodies the traveler-merchant of the **Islamic Golden Age**: piety, greed, courage, and the inability to sit still once rich. Behind the monsters, we read an allegory of fortune rising and falling.
The story opens in Baghdad. **Sindbad the Sailor**, now old and wealthy, recounts his ordeals to a porter also named Sindbad (sometimes Hindbad). The class contrast is immediate.

blocks.caption: Baghdad, departure and return point for Sindbad's journeys.

blocks.text: Each journey follows the same mechanics: weariness of sedentary life, departure from the port of, shipwreck, survival in an unknown land, return loaded with treasures. The number seven, loaded with meaning in the [[Basra]], gives the series an initiatory dimension: from imprudence to wisdom. [[Islamic cosmology]]
The **Rock** (or Rokh), a bird whose wingspan obscures the sun, has left its mark on the world's imagination. We see the echo of stories of Arab travelers on the coasts of East Africa.

blocks.caption: The Roc, giant bird of Sindbad's travels.

blocks.text: The Roc is probably inspired by the **Aepyornis**, an elephant bird from Madagascar that disappeared around the year 1000. Its eggs were up to 150 times the volume of a chicken egg.

Sindbad also faces the **Old Man of the Sea**, who clings to his back, and the **turtle island**, deceptive ground. The **valley of diamonds**, where meat is thrown to stick the gems, is already circulating among the Ancients. The marvelous sediments of the centuries of . [[Medieval Arab trade routes]]

sections.title: A fantastic bestiary between myth and reality

blocks.text: The setting is historic. In the 8th and 9th centuries, sailors from Basra and Siraf dominated the Indian Ocean. Sindbad's stops evoke real places:  (Ceylon) for spices, South-East Asia for camphor, the coasts for pearls. [[Serendib]]

blocks.caption: Arab ships on the Indian Ocean routes.

blocks.text: Sindbad is not a warrior: he is a merchant-adventurer, a prestigious status in a society that values ​​commerce. There we find the monsoon, ships sewn with coconut fibers rather than nailed. Western parallel: , which describes Asia in facts, where Sindbad paints it in wonders. [[Marco Polo (Western parallel)]]

sections.title: The mirror of the Golden Age of Arab trade

blocks.text: Translated in the 18th century by **Antoine Galland**, travel nourishes the European , from Defoe to Jules Verne. The cinema often makes him a privateer in the service of princesses. Error: Sindbad is initially a city dweller from Baghdad, surviving through faith and ingenuity. [[Adventure novel]]
The name Sindbad would evoke the “prince of the Sindh river”, the Indus, at the crossroads of the Arab and Indian worlds.
**Sinbad** embodies the Islamic maritime golden age in **seven** cyclical voyages: the Rock and the diamonds mask a reality, that of the Arab merchants masters of the Indian Ocean.
